question.text: A commodity has a spot price of Rs 10,000. The annual interest rate is 8% and holding period is 6 months. Using simple cost-of-carry (no storage), what is the fair futures price?

explanation.text: The Logic: F = S + C = 10,000 + (10,000 × 0.08 × 6/12) = 10,000 + 400 = Rs 10,400. The Trap: Rs 10,800 uses a full year of interest. Rs 10,000 ignores the cost of carry. Rs 10,200 uses 3 months instead of 6. Note: Cash-and-carry arbitrage arises when the futures price is more than spot price plus the cost of carry. If the futures premium is below the carry, buying spot and selling futures is not an arbitrage.
